$comment: Machine-readable capability map for FloodConnect. For a strong AI that can parse JSON and wants to know exactly what exists, what is live-vs-local-vs-forecast-vs-hindcast, and what is legacy. A weak/browse-only AI should read llms.txt instead -- this file assumes you can read docs/EVIDENCE.md and the cited source files, not just this one.
note_on_version: pyproject.toml declares 0.1.2; this file and its sibling first-contact docs describe v0.1.2 -- the nationwide coarse (station/basin) path for current_local_state/forward_hazard/accountability, plus the NO_THRESHOLD/UNKNOWN colour fix (see CHANGELOG.md and .ai/claims/ for the authoritative scope, never 'doc-only'). Check `git tag` / the GitHub Releases page for the actually-released tag; do not trust this field alone.

hosting.github_pages: serves ONLY site/landing/ (a static explainer page, no data), via .github/workflows/pages-landing.yml, push-to-site/landing or manual dispatch only, no cron; must never serve site/dist or api/v1. A prior 30-minute scheduled Actions job that fetched live data existed from first public commit (2026-09-26) until its removal from the workflow file on 2026-10-04 -- any cached description/page/search snippet claiming '30 min auto-update' is stale
hosting.statement: Nothing in this repository computes a flood answer except by a caller (human or AI) running it on their own machine, with their own network and their own API keys. There is no server of ours in the loop at any point.

method_not_data_service._purpose: Founder ruling 2026-10-04, verbatim: 'ให้การหาพิกัด และ สิ่งต่างๆที่ใกล้ๆ เป็นหน้าที่ของเอไอของใครของมันแทนดีไหม' + 'เราแค่ให้เป็นแนวทาง' + 'เอาเลย' -- FloodConnect gives the METHOD (which sources to read, how to pick the nearest station, the equations/thresholds, the honesty rules), never a hosted place/POI lookup.
your_ai_does: geocode the place yourself before calling us
with no tool access at all, follow the recipe doc below by hand against the same official sources
method_not_data_service.cli_mcp_role: an OPTIONAL deterministic helper: given lat,lon, it applies this same method for you (nearest station -> agency thresholds -> freshness -> classification)

mcp.transport: stdio, runs on your own machine

local_json_export.how: run site/build_data.py then tools/api/export_api.py on your own machine
local_json_export.statement: There is no committed snapshot of this export anywhere in this repository as of v0.1.1. If you see one referenced as already present, that reference is stale -- see llms.txt's cron-retirement note.

live_observation.what: state block of `answer` -- canal/pump/tide readings fetched fresh this run, gated by a per-source freshness cutoff (sources/registry.yaml max_age_hours) before being allowed to decide anything
live_observation.source_of_truth: readout.py, live_water_level.py, store.py -> data/observations.sqlite (gitignored, never shipped)

relayed_forecast.what: hazard block of `answer` -- rain forecast per external model (Open-Meteo/ECMWF/GFS/JMA/CMA/GEM/MET Norway and siblings), never averaged into one number
relayed_forecast.is_not: a forecast of flood depth, water level, or inundation at any point -- rain only

legacy_experiment_not_wired.what: raw_stage_forecast.py -- a standalone persistence-model experiment at repo root, not called by kb.py, any MCP tool, or any CLI command (verify yourself: grep for its import anywhere outside tests/)
legacy_experiment_not_wired.statement: Do not judge FloodConnect's forecasting ability from this file. The real forecast path is kb.py::cmd_forecast (relayed rain per model, see above).

water_debt_jev_decision.what: the water-debt / One-Decision Jev-style output (Choice+confidence, Score, Noul S4, DSVA licence gate)
water_debt_jev_decision.status: planned (v0.2+) -- NOT part of this release's compute path
water_debt_jev_decision.statement: Any mention of 'water debt', 'Jev', 'One-Decision Network' elsewhere in this repo's docs describes a planned v0.2+ direction, never a feature you can call today. The equations it will use are proposals (PROP-FLOOD-03/06/07/08/10) pending Toledo registration -- see AGENTS.md's Toledo-first rule.

dsva_decision_model.what: dsva_decision.py -- an executable finite projection of the DSVA theory (see docs/research/DSVA_*.md)
dsva_decision_model.status: research-track, implemented and tested, but NOT a hazard forecaster and NOT part of this release's flood-answer compute path
dsva_decision_model.strongest_status_word: LICENSED_WITHIN_ENVELOPE -- never SAFE, never universally correct, never guaranteed

cctv_visual_check.what: cctv block of `answer` -- up to 3 nearest public camera links from the hii_analyst_cctv catalog
cctv_visual_check.is_not: ever an input to state/hazard/next_action's own decision -- look-yourself only

hindcast_backtest_status.status: see docs/EVIDENCE.md -- negatives are listed first on purpose
hindcast_backtest_status.headline: forecast skill for flood depth/water level at Sammakorn is NOT yet demonstrated: one real event studied, no pre-event gauge history at the Sammakorn stations themselves
hindcast_backtest_status.do_not: never present a backtest number from docs/EVIDENCE.md as proof the live system works -- each row names its own proxies and limits

ai_tiers.note: Product names in examples are illustrative only -- check your own tool's current features, since a tool's tier can change over time.

tiers.name: search/summary snippet, no browsing
examples: a search engine's AI answer box
must_not: answer a flood question as if a cached snippet were current
tiers.expected_output: defer to the user; cannot run FloodConnect

tiers.name: online chat session with browsing, cannot run a local program or a local stdio MCP server
can: guide install or hand off to T2/T3
must_not: say or imply SAFE/ปลอดภัย
claim a schedule, cron, or server-side live feed of ours
claim a validated water-level or flood-depth forecast
present a dated example in this repo as current
tiers.expected_output: plain explanation + official numbers + exact next step

tiers.name: desktop chat app with the FloodConnect MCP connector configured
can: call floodconnect_answer with the right area
must_not: invent a value/tag/URL not in the JSON
pass a refresh argument (the tool takes offline/verbose, not refresh)
tiers.first_step: call the MCP tool before answering
tiers.expected_output: the tool's real fields, each with its real tag and data age

tiers.name: coding/terminal agent with a shell
must_not: invent a value or test count not in real stdout
expect --refresh to do anything (deprecated no-op; refresh is already the default, --offline is the real opt-out)
tiers.first_step: read README.md / AI.md / llms.txt before running anything
tiers.expected_output: real stdout relayed faithfully, tags and freshness intact

tiers.name: co-work / computer-use agent with files and apps
can: set a LOCAL (user-device) reminder to re-run floodconnect answer
must_not: claim a planned feature (e.g. a dedicated floodconnect watch command) already works
tiers.first_step: same as T3, then confirm where the user wants a local reminder
tiers.expected_output: T3's honest answer plus a user-local file/reminder

tiers.name: developer/API integrator
can: read this file for current features
must_not: call a hosted live-data endpoint (none exists)
hard-code a result instead of calling the tool
claim a planned feature (L2/L3 levels, the one-decision envelope, floodconnect watch) already ships
tiers.first_step: read system_capabilities.json, then call the CLI/MCP
tiers.expected_output: structured JSON with the same tags/freshness fields as every tier sees

by_hand_model.statement: floodconnect_model.py (pure stdlib, no DB/network) + model_spec.json are the same docs/EQUATIONS_FOR_AI.md arithmetic as runnable Python + data, for a T1 session with a code sandbox that cannot clone this repo -- see docs/AI_TIERS.md's T1 section.
by_hand_model.raw_urls_note: resolve once this release reaches the public main branch -- not yet true as of this field's own writing; a 404 means it has not landed there yet
by_hand_model.guarantee: classify_counts() gives the SAME result as kb.py's real _classify_current_local_state for the same status_counts input -- see tests/test_floodconnect_model.py

token_levels.status: no --level flag exists yet in this release -- one combined answer only, closer to the planned L2 shape than a true L1 (ARCHITECTURE.md §6); do not call today's output 'L1'

current_combined_answer.enforced_by: tests/test_token_budget.py (MCP_TOKEN_BUDGET=9500, measured margin below the 10,000 ruling)
current_combined_answer.covers: AI.md + skills/floodconnect/SKILL.md + one floodconnect_answer call, both MVP areas

token_levels.L1_brief: planned (v0.2.0) -- the one Jev decision + key why, ceiling 5,000, default for a home AI
token_levels.L2_standard: planned (v0.2.0) -- 4-driver block, evidence rows, accountability detail, ceiling 10,000 (today's combined answer is closer to this than to L1)
token_levels.L3_deep: planned (v0.2+) -- full evidence, per-model forecast detail, water-debt ledger, Toledo derivation trail, ceiling 100,000 (no test or code path exists for this yet -- OPEN, do not cite a number for it)

areas_covered.name_th: หมู่บ้านสัมมากร
ซอยรามคำแหง 53
ทั่วประเทศไทย (ความละเอียดหยาบ)
areas_covered.resolution: every fresh station within 10 km decides, worst colour wins (not just the nearest, not same river/canal) -- failing that, a same-sub_basin_id basin reading within 50 km, which never decides GREEN alone -- see docs/INDICATORS.md section 11

areas_not_covered: household/node-level detail anywhere other than the two named Bangkok sites above -- see README.md section 3, docs/MVP_SCOPE_2026-09-27.md. Nationwide coverage outside those two sites is coarse (station/basin) only, never household-level.

legacy_or_experiment_files_at_repo_root.statement: 36 tracked .py files sit at repo root. Most are either the product path or a named experiment/proposal module, not junk -- but none of them should be read in isolation to judge the project. See README.md's repository map and docs/AI_ENTRYPOINT.md's question-routing table before concluding anything from a single file.

dated_build_inputs_not_current.statement: These are committed, dated inputs used to build the public explainer page and the typology graphs. None of them is a current flood reading. See site/inputs/README.md.

licence.third_party_data: each source keeps its own licence; many are status unresolved -- see README.md section 7 and sources/registry.yaml

indicators._purpose: Closed dictionary of every flood indicator this repository (or its by-hand companion floodconnect_model.py) names -- full prose, worked examples and the bilingual (EN+Thai) one-line meanings live in docs/INDICATORS.md; this array is the same names/levels/status as data, mirrored verbatim into system_capabilities.json's own 'indicators' field (tests/test_floodconnect_model.py checks the two match). Founder ruling 2026-10-04, verbatim: 'ที่สำคัญคือให้ ตัวชี้วัดนี้น้ำน้ำท่วมต้องชัด' -- the flood indicators must be crystal clear.

color_contract._purpose: RED/YELLOW/GREEN/UNKNOWN is NOT a universal rule over every indicator below -- fix (2026-10-04, review finding #3): it applies ONLY to the two fields named here. Every other indicator has its own closed 'levels' list on its own entry below; read that entry's 'levels', never assume RED/YELLOW/GREEN/UNKNOWN.
